correctness.rationale: The proof reduces ternary class sizes to a weighted count of binary parity patterns. The syndrome-parity identity and cyclic-rotation increment are derived explicitly; prime rotation orbits make weighted and signed residue sums uniform away from the two constant words. Solving those two sums yields the four formulas. The accompanying verifier checks the critical identities and formulas for \(p\in\{3,5,7,11\}\) and directly verifies two-consecutive-deletion covering for every syndrome class at \(p\in\{3,5,7\}\). The infinite covering assertion itself is sourced to Xie--Sun--Ge Theorem VI.4.

evidence: Xie--Sun--Ge prove covering for all q in their lifted construction and give an averaging upper bound.

evidence: The source averaging bound guarantees only that some class has size at most \(3^p/(2p)\).
The exact formula identifies all \(2p\) class sizes and all \(p-1\) minimizers.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The exact distribution is strictly stronger than the averaging consequence within the same explicit construction and is not implied by direct q-ary DVT size formulas.

evidence: The inspected source statements give the generic size bound and exact direct-DVT cardinalities, respectively; no ternary parity-lift prime-length table or four-case formula was located.

originality.rationale: The closest 2026 paper supplies the parity-and-checksum covering construction and only an averaging cardinality bound; its ternary specialization leaves a weighted differential-VT syndrome distribution that is not evaluated there. The 2025 DVT cardinality paper concerns direct q-ary DVT classes, not parity-lift preimages with nonuniform ternary lift weights. General deletion-covering literature does not imply the exact four-level distribution. Targeted repository and web searches found no statement of the formula.
residual_risks: No database search can prove novelty; an unindexed note could contain an equivalent weighted-syndrome calculation.

value.rationale: The 2026 construction leaves its ternary syndrome parameter to averaging. The exact distribution identifies every optimal parameter inside the construction, quantifies the improvement over the generic bound, and exposes a rotation-orbit mechanism that can guide analysis of other small alphabets. This is a natural structural invariant of the newly introduced nonbinary two-burst covering family rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
